findings.description: Genji tells the servants to hurry the dinner service already underway. Both editions tell them to prepare the dinner table instead, changing the task from serving the meal to table preparation. MG also describes service timing as timing while setting the table; UP correctly describes dish-serving timing there.

急ぎますよ…！」

Just then, the crisp sound of hands clapping twice rang through the hallway.
They all turned around at once to see Gohda coming out of the dining hall.
"Okay, everyone.
When serving a dinner, proper timing while setting the table is essential.
Please immediately see to setting out the soup.

Kanon reluctantly turned away and returned his expression to normal.

Hurry...!"
Gohda grabbed the serving cart from Shannon and steadily pushed it towards the kitchen.

findings.description: Krauss says the gloomy atmosphere makes Gohda’s accomplished dinner lack savor. UP says the dinner has been poorly received, replacing the depressed atmosphere with an assertion about the diners’ reception of the meal. MG preserves the gloomy atmosphere.

findings.alternative: Retirement pay can support old age, but the source ties the joke to many years of service and does not describe Beatrice as old. The joke’s broad retirement image remains.
